CITY OF ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY
  COMMISSION
  THURSDAY, JULY 10, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
Environmental Sustainability Commission will be held on Thursday, July 10,
2025 at 6:00 p.m. in Conference Room A, on the second floor of the Alhambra
City Hall, 111 S. First St., Alhambra, California, pursuant to the order of the
Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission Secretary.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto, incorporated herein by
reference and made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  Latoya Waters,
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability
  Commission Secretary

Notice No. N2M25-90
Posted: 7/7/2025
   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  July 10, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Katie Chan, Scott Chan, Xana Hermosillo, Michael Scaduto

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve 05-08-2025 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Staff will provide an update on the Sustainability Plan.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION
  The Environmental Sustainability Commission will discuss action items for the next meeting.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required.

  V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit
  all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior to the
  meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business of the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5) minutes.

  VI.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

  VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, September 11, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

  If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
  the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
  make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

  If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
  heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
  which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard
  under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on May 8, 2025

The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
order at 6:00 p.m. on May 8, 2025.

I.  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Katie Chan, Scott Chan, Xana Hermosillo,
  Michael Scaduto

  Staff Present: Katie Martel, Sustainability Analyst and Latoya Waters, Deputy
  Director of Utilities serving as Commission Secretary

  Members of the Public:
  Lola Armendariz - Resident
  Albert Viera – Resident
  Duke – API Forward
  Cecilia – API Forward Movement

II. VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES
  The Commission reviewed and approved the minutes from the previous meeting
  on March 13, 2025.

  Commissioner S. Chan motioned to approve the meeting minutes from March 13,
  2025. Commissioner Hermosillo seconded the motion. Commissioners K. Chan,
  S. Chan, and Hermosillo voted in favor to approve said minutes. Commissioner
  Scaduto abstained. Motion passed.

III. GREEN STREET DEMONSTRATION PROJECT ON MAIN STREET
  UPDATE
  Update of the Green Street Demonstration Project on Main Street provided by
  staff (L. Waters).
  • Background – Identified as a “large scale project” to mitigate stormwater
  under the Enhanced Watershed Management Plan (EWMP), required
  under the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES)
  Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Permit.
  o The “large scare projects” were prioritized in the City of Alhambra
  (City) Stormwater Master Plan.
  o The Green Streets Project initiated with the development of a
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on May 8, 2025

  “Feasibility Study” – funded by LA County
•  Project Highlights – Drainage Area = 40 acres, 4 drywells north of Main
  Street (Birch and Grand), 20,000 sf bioretention areas, Planting 34 new
  trees, Pedestrian Enhancements (Separate Project), Primary Objective:
  Improve Water Quality, Secondary Objectives: Increased Greenery,
  Pedestrian Safety.
•  Dry Well features – subsurface storage facility and will recharge
  groundwater sources
•  Bioretention Cells – Shallow, planted depressions geared to treat and
  manage stormwater runoff.
•  Benefits – Water Quality/Environmental: Improve water quality, reduce
  discharge of bacteria, trash, and debris, improve public health by reducing
  pollutants, increase local water supply (groundwater recharge), reduce
  irrigation demand by implementing native landscaping.
•  Benefits – Community: beautification of Main Street with increased urban
  greening, reduce carbon through new trees and landscape, reduce urban
  heat island effects, habitat improvements with native landscaping,
  potential economic enhancements with beautification, create opportunities
  for education and outreach.
•  Anticipated schedule –
  o Preliminary Feasibility - July 2023
  o Environmental (CEQA) Public Review - April 2025
  o Complete Design and Environmental - July 2025
  o Bidding - August 2025
  o Construction Start - Fall 2025
  o Construction Duration - 15 months
•  Funding –
  o California Natural Resources Agency (CNRA): $3,005,040 for Urban
  Greening
  o Safe Clean Water Program (SCWP) Infrastructure Program:
  $2,027,000
  o SCWP Municipal Funds
  o City of Alhambra
•  Additional information can be found on the City’s website.
•  Questions:
  o Commissioner Scaduto – congratulated the City in securing the Urban
  Greening Grant. Is the project funded or recommended for funding?
  Upper LA River?
   L. Water – It is recommended for funding. Yes (Upper LA
  River)
  o Commissioner Scaduto – How long has it taken from when it (the
  project) is approved in the SIP (Stormwater Investment Plan) to
  executing the Transfer Agreement with the County? More or less than

  Page 2 of 8
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on May 8, 2025

  one-year?
   L. Water – Less than one-year? We are anticipating going
  to the Regional Oversight Committee (ROC) in June and
  possibly to the Board in August/September.
o  Commissioner Scaduto – Given this is a quick project is there
  consideration for the City to apply for O&M (Operation and
  Maintenance) funds this round or the next?
   L. Water – If we (City) do consider O&M, it would be next
  round.
o  Commissioner S. Chan – How was this area chosen for this project?
   L. Waters – Good drainage area was the main
  consideration. Other locations were examined but none of
  the other sites proposed were able to deliver the large
  drainage and capture area.
o  Commissioner S. Chan – What does it (the project) look like “during
  construction”? Will residents know what’s going on?
   L. Waters – Yes. we are required to have signage during
  construction and will display contact information for
  questions or concerns. We will also continue educational
  outreach regarding the project through the construction
  phase.
o  A. Viera – How do you decide which plants to use?
   L. Waters - the landscape specialist on the consultant team
  designed and selected the project planting.
o  Commissioner Hermosillo – Are there any other areas considered for
  projects?
   L. Waters - Story Park – infiltration chamber to treat runoff
  as well as divert some of the San Pasqual Wash flow.
  Burke Heritage Park – Dry well features to capture runoff
  and provide park enhancements.
o  Commissioner K. Chan – Would there be additional opportunities for
  constituents to comment on the project?
   L. Waters – the City had two (2) public outreach meetings
  at Reese Hall, One (1) at the actual project site, one (1) at
  Emery Park Elementary School and tabled at the City
  Farmer’s Market and Eco Fair.
o  Commissioner K. Chan – Any general comments received from the
  Commissioners or the Public today be considered?
   L. Waters – We received some information at the last
  outreach meeting (which was scheduled at the same time as
  our March Environmental Sustainability Meeting). Those
  comments were considered and reflected in the 90% plans.
  That was the last opportunity for public comment.

  Page 3 of 8

  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on May 8, 2025

  o L. Armendariz – Where does Burke come in?
   L. Waters - We will have a xeriscape garden, bioretention
  and other features.
  o L. Armendariz – Will there be tanks stored under Burke Park?
   L. Waters - No tanks at Burke Park. Stormwater will be
  diverted from a County line to a seasonal wetland.
   L. Waters - Story Park will have an infiltration chamber.
  o L. Armendariz – why were the two (2) smallest parks chosen? What is
  the capacity of the tanks? What do we do if the system malfunctions
  during an earthquake? What is digging up the soil going to do to those
  well-established trees?
   L. Waters – No large chambers or tanks will be placed in
  Burke Heritage Park.
  o L. Armendariz – Native plants do not generate enough oxygen. They
  are decorative but emphasis should not be placed on their preference.
  o Commissioner S. Chan – Does the gas station on the corner of Main
  and Fremont play into rainwater capture?
   L. Waters – No. we are not disturbing the area near the gas
  station. We will also avoid all underground utilities in the
  project area.
  o Commissioner Scaduto – How does the City typically conduct
  outreach?
   L. Waters – This being a “demonstration” project (first of
  its kind) we began with postcard mailers in the three (3)
  prominent languages in Alhambra for the first two (2)
  rounds, the third-round staff and I canvassed the area to
  discuss the project with local business as well as
  pedestrians in the area. We also placed project information
  on the website, displayed large poster boards at City Hall
  and the library as well as social media platforms.
  o L. Armendariz – Are you doing any outreach to the immediate
  community around the project?
   L. Waters – Yes. We sent out direct postcard mailers and
  tabled at the project site.
  o L. Armendariz – What are we doing at Burke Heritage?
  o A. Viera – the paper “Around Alhambra” is this in there?
   K. Martel – it was in there during the time of our townhall
  meetings. It is a Chamber of Commerce publication.

IV. SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  K. Martel, Sustainability Analyst provided an update on the City’s Sustainability
  Plan, currently in development process.

  Page 4 of 8
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on May 8, 2025

The Sustainability Plan (Plan) has been in development for the better part of about
a year or so, we are actively engaged in developing the first comprehensive
Sustainability Plan for the City. In March, staff provided an update of the townhall
meetings. We are collecting more data to gather as much input as possible from the
community. The City developed an online questionnaire which is available on the
“Sustainable Alhambra” webpage. It is offered in English, Spanish, and Chinese.
It is a bit more specific, asking questions such as what type of programming would
people like? What are their priorities? What are they (residents and/or businesses)
interested in doing on their own property? Are you interested in turning hardscape
into greenspace? Are you interested in planting a tree on your property? We are
looking to keep the surveys open until June. We are utilizing partner support – City
newsletter, Library newsletter, and APIFM. We encourage the Commissioners to
take a look at the survey and share it with your networks and neighborhoods. All
of the data gathered will be used in the draft plan to cover all nine (9) sectors of the
Plan. These sectors can vary from air quality, greening and open space to economic
sustainability and sustainability culture. These changes provided by the community
are really social/behavior changes, however we want to include part of plan is
focused on education and outreach regarding the needs of the City. Also, encourage
household level adoption and the broader community too. The draft Plan should be
available by Fall 2025 (October). Once the Plan is drafted it will be presented
before Council first, followed by presentations to the Commissioners and public
feedback. The City will take into consideration the Commissioners meeting
schedules for comments.
  • Questions:
  o Commissioner S. Chan – Is it possible to add questions to the survey?
  Adding demographics (age) to get a better idea of who is filling out
  the survey?
   K. Martel – That is a good point. We do ask about district
  but not age specifically. I can talk to our consultants about
  adding on supplemental questions.
   At our Eco Fair we had a poster with the nine (9) sectors
  identified and asked attendees to place a star accordingly.
  we are also looking to have a star board displayed at the
  Library as we have a pretty heavy high school/student foot
  traffic. This can be incorporated as a “popsicle day” or
  “chips day’ to gather more participation.
  o Commissioner K. Chan – What is the anticipated date for that
  (Library star board exercise)?
   K. Martel – there is not a scheduled date as of right now
  but we will let the Commissioners know when the date is
  confirmed.
  o Commissioner Scaduto – Is it possible to combine similar efforts

  Page 5 of 8
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on May 8, 2025

  coordinated by the Safe Clean Water Program Watershed
  Coordinators?
   K. Martel – We had the Council for Watershed Health
  (current Watershed Coordinators) attend our townhall
  meetings.
  o  Commissioner K. Chan – Will the consultants return to present before
  the commissioners?
   K. Martel – Yes. After the consultants present to Council
  they will return for a presentation to the Commissioners.
  o  L. Armendariz – Will all of the outreach be online?
   K. Martel – Not necessarily, we have done in-person
  meetings in each council district, we have done local
  events such as the Eco Fair and Alhambra Recycles.
  o  L Armendariz – How did you get out information where the meeting
  will be held?
   K. Martel – postcards and flyers handed out and
  digitalized. The postcard activity allowed the City to gather
  about 700 direct contacts of interested individuals.
  o  L Armendariz – suggestion to add local event information on the City
  Council agenda to avoid excluding people (that are) not on social
  media.

V. AIR QUALITY AND AIR FILTER STUDY UPDATE
Asian Pacific Islander Forward Movement (APIFM) will provide and update on the Air
Quality and Air Filter Study.

  •  Just finalized two (2) studies based on air quality in Alhambra and
  Monterey Park. Between 2023-2024 APIFM implemented these studies in
  coordination with the USC Environmental Justice Lab.
  •  Study 1 - used purple air filters) to collect yearlong data:
  o Identified four (4) Hotspot locations;
   Main/Garfield
   Mark Kimpel High School
   Fremont Elementary
   East LA Community College
  o July 5the was recorded as the highest level of PM2.5 (particulate
  matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers or less)
  o PM2.5 levels were also higher during time of heavy traffic (6-7am
  and 4-6pm)
  •  Study 2 – With feedback from residents the targeted areas were identified.
  Focused on SB535 designated communities, placing indoor and outdoor
  sensors in 10 homes. Testing DIY vs commercial filters. Held public
  workshops and partnered with local youth:

  Page 6 of 8
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on May 8, 2025

  o Indoor vs outdoor air quality and air effectiveness
  o (October 2023 – March 2024): 3 commercial brand air hosts, 3 DIY
  air filter hosts, 4 control groups (no filter).
  o (April 2024 – July 2024): Extended and increased DIY filter group to
  6.
  o Identified daily trends - Sunday is the lowest recorded day of the
  week.
  •  Continue monitoring: www.map.purpleair.com
  •  Questions:
  o Commissioner S. Chan – Would the City be open to hosting a sensor
  at locations such as Almansor Park?
  o How long did the DIY filter last and what was the base cost?
   Duke – API Forward - Base cost: (commercial) Amazon
  for approximately $100 each. DIY was approximately $40-
  $50. Purchasing in bulk with provided more cost savings.
   DIY seemed to work better, but they are considered big and
  clunky. Dirt and build up are more visible with DIY
  models.
   Longevity depends on activity within the home, pets,
  stove/kitchen usage. About 3-4 months. Commercial units
  indicate a 6-month filter change out, but the study
  demonstrates that may be too long.
  o Commissioner Hermosillo thanked APIFM for attending and
  presenting at this meeting. Hopefully we can continue further efforts
  to monitor local air quality.
  o Commissioner K. Chan asked to be updated regarding future projects
  and efforts.

VI. ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY DISCUSSION
  Commissioner Scaduto expressed interest in learning about what projects are
  listed in the City’s Stormwater Master Plan. Curiosity to see how the
  Transportation and Stormwater Master Plan align. Also, would like to see if
  Almansor Park was considered.

  L. Waters – responded regarding Almansor Park. This project was initially
  considered as a potential project site and partnership with neighboring cities.
  However, the cost was astronomical and it was a former dump site which provides
  limited opportunity for water quality enhancement.

  K. Martel - We have quite a few plans in the City, we have our Hazard Mitigation
  Plan that is out for public comment. There is synergy between the plans and
  departments coming together to amplify the benefits of projects. Transportation is
  a huge element of these efforts.

  Commissioner Scaduto - Has there been some consideration to incorporate local
  schools into future plans?

  Commissioner K. Chan – anymore outreach before draft release?
  K. Martel - We do not have any planned meetings at the moment.

VII.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Two (2) comments cards were received.

  1. Albert Viera – Planting native plants and edible plants: I noticed many people
  want to garden but do not have the space and others have the space but are
  unable to garden. Is it possible to connect these two (2) groups? Providing
  opportunity for native and edible plants would be advantageous for the City.
  Also, incentives should be in place to encourage people to use native plants
  when retrieving building permits.
  2. Lola Armendariz – Green Street: (leaf) blowers are the worse thing we have in
  the City. South Pasadena switched to batteries due to the noise. What goes up
  must come down, down to your lawn, cars, your homes. We are breathing it
  and it will also come down on our hair, our body. There is a vacuum that can
  be used, it is rather large. These (leaf) blowers do not promote good air quality.
  We should address this here.

VIII.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

IX. ADJOURNMENT
  Commissioner K. Chan adjourned the meeting at 7:16 p.m.
